_whose: This file belongs to the person who runs Granite Record, like member_corrections.json and place_corrections.json. Claude drafted the 24 entries below on 24 September 2026 for that person's review: 18 from the phantom-sitting investigation of 23 September, and 6 more where the House Journal and the roll call agree with each other against the docket. narrative.py applies every entry until the person removes it. Read them; the file is yours.
_what: Dates the General Court's docket states wrongly ('dates'), and rows it files under the wrong bill ('misfiled'), corrected by a person, with the evidence for each correction beside it. This file is edited by hand. No generator writes it, and preflight fails if any build_* or fetch_* script opens it for writing.
_why: A floor action's date decides which sitting it belongs to, and a sitting page is built for every date that carries one. A single mistyped date therefore publishes a sitting that never happened -- 'The House, Saturday 19 September 2026' -- and takes the action off the day it did happen. A correction is made only where the record settles it and nothing points the other way: the journal the row cites, the other rows that cite the same journal, the time the row was written, and where one exists the roll call's own timestamp, which comes from the voting system rather than the docket.
_how: narrative.py is the only reader. It matches an entry on session (the docket's first column), bill, body and the text of the docket row (source_says), with runs of spaces collapsed on both sides; uses corrected_to as the event's date; and keeps the docket's own date beside it as date_as_recorded, with 'note' shown under the docket line on the bill's page. An entry whose row no longer reads as source_says is reported by narrative.py and NOT applied, and preflight fails on it while that term's docket is on disk: it means the General Court has changed the row and this file is now the thing that is stale. narrative.py also warns about any row of the same bill that carries an entry's mistyped date and journal but has no entry of its own. A 'misfiled' entry is matched the same way, on session, bill, body and source_says: narrative.py takes that row out of the bill's history -- its sentence, its journey and the sitting it would put the bill on -- and keeps it in the bill's list of the docket's own lines with 'note' beneath it; belongs_to names the bill the row belongs to, and 'note_there' is shown beneath that bill's own row of the same action (belongs_to_says). A misfiled entry that matches no row is reported and not applied, and preflight fails on it in the same way.
_not_for: Business a chamber did while standing in recess of an earlier sitting (HJ 14 of 2024 prints non-concurrences of 24, 28 and 29 May under the 23 May sitting), dispositions under a joint rule, and database-era rows dated by the moment they were entered. Those are not typing errors and are left for the person to decide; preflight lists them as known doubtful days.
